precepts.text: Sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past. The margin note points that fast to the tenth day of the seventh month, Leviticus 23:27. Paul kept the day of atonement, but was he sacrificing on the day? No, because he had faith in Christ.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.
precepts.why:
“Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them”. The margin note beside “the fast” points it to the tenth day of the seventh month, Leviticus 23:27 and 29: the day of atonement.

So Paul kept the day of atonement. But was Paul sacrificing on that day? No. Why? Because he had that faith in Christ. He fasted, but he was not offering an animal on that day.

That is the line Colossians 2:23 draws. Neglecting of the body, the fasting, is not the problem; Paul kept the fast himself. The problem is the men who used a show of wisdom to pull the believers back under the carnal ordinances of sacrifice after Christ had come.
